Documents circulate by email and nobody knows whose desk the approval is stuck on.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Answers about automation, pricing and how we'd work together
faq.q1: How long does an implementation take?
faq.a1: A simple process takes 1–2 weeks. A more complex one, integrating several systems, takes 3–4 weeks. I always start with whatever proves value fastest.
faq.a2: Implementing a single process starts at a fixed price agreed before we start — never "ask for a quote". Full pricing is public on the /cennik page.
faq.q3: Do I need to understand the underlying tools?
faq.a3: No. We talk about your process and the hours you could get back. I pick the tools and take responsibility for them.
faq.a4: Automation left unattended eventually breaks as the systems around it change. I offer a monthly care plan to keep it running.
faq.q5: Who actually does the work — a company or one person?
faq.a5: One person, from the first call through implementation and ongoing care. Your project doesn't get handed off between a salesperson and a different implementer.
faq.q6: Can I see pricing before talking to you?
faq.a6: Yes — pricing is public. Book a free call once you've seen it, and we'll talk about your specific process.

rpa.faq_title: Frequently asked questions about task automation

faq.q: Do I need to change my existing systems?
faq.a: No. Automation works on top of your existing systems — no software swap or vendor approval needed.

faq.q: What happens if a system the robot works with changes?
faq.a: The automation needs updating. That's why I offer a care plan — I monitor changes and react before the process stops.

faq.q: How long does it take to implement?
faq.a: A simple process is ready in 1–2 weeks. Something more complex, with several integrations, takes 3–4 weeks.

workflow.h1: Workflow automation – no more manual handoffs
workflow.subtitle: I connect systems, apps and people into one coherent, automated process.
workflow.cta_subtitle: Book a free call and show me your processes.
workflow.s1_p1: Workflow automation is designing and implementing flows that connect different systems, apps and teams into one coherent, automated process. Instead of manually passing data between applications, your systems talk to each other automatically.
workflow.s1_p2: In practice, data entered once in one place ends up wherever it's needed — no copy-pasting, no email attachments, no "has someone already done this?".
benefits: Eliminates manual data handoffs between systems
Full visibility into the status of every task
Easy to extend as the company grows

integration.h1: System integration – connecting ERP, CRM and databases
integration.subtitle: I build bridges between your systems, creating one coherent ecosystem with automatic data exchange.
integration.cta_subtitle: Describe your systems and I'll propose the right connection.
integration.s1_p1: 5–50 person companies typically run a handful of applications: ERP, CRM, email, warehouse, sales platform. Without integration, someone manually moves data between them, which creates errors, delays and frustration.
integration.s1_p2: I connect your systems through APIs, webhooks and dedicated middleware so data flows automatically, in real time — no more monthly export to a spreadsheet.
benefits: Data stays current across every system
Faster flow of information and decisions
One consistent customer view for the whole team

ai.subtitle: I build AI assistants that analyze documents, answer customer questions and keep an eye on your data.
ai.cta_title: Ready for an AI agent at your company?
ai.cta_subtitle: Let's find out which process would benefit most from an AI agent.
ai.s1_title: What an AI agent actually does
ai.s1_p1: Unlike a plain RPA robot, an AI agent understands the content of a document or question rather than just clicking predefined spots. It can read an invoice in any format, answer a customer in natural language, or summarize a long document.
ai.s1_p2: It doesn't replace the expert in your company. It takes the first pass at a large volume of data — documents, messages, questions — and only passes forward what actually needs a human decision.

cennik_page.subtitle: Prices stated upfront, never "ask for a quote". Below you'll find implementation cost, care plans and the ROI calculator.
cennik_page.tier3_text: Some clients qualify for public co-funding on training and consulting.
cennik_page.why_title: Why I don't take implementations under a certain price
cennik_page.why_text: Below that level there isn't enough room for a real process audit, error handling in the automation, and training your team. A cheaper offer usually means one of those got skipped — and that's the part that comes back to bite you when the process breaks after a month.

faq.q: Is the price fixed, or can it grow during the project?
faq.a: The price agreed at the start is fixed. If the audit reveals a bigger scope than assumed, I tell you before work starts, not during it.

faq.q: What if the process turns out to be harder than expected?
faq.a: That's exactly what the audit is for — I recommend starting there if the process is complex or spans several systems.
No, but without it automation tends to break over time as external systems change — so I do recommend it.

faq.q: Do you issue a VAT invoice?
faq.a: Yes, every engagement is billed with a VAT invoice.

about_page.subtitle: I'm a software developer by trade, but I've also run smaller businesses myself — I know first-hand how much time and attention manual work and document overload eat up in a small company.
about_page.why_p1: I'm a software developer by trade — automation, Python and system integrations are my everyday craft, not a service bolted on for marketing. But before I started building automations for other people, I ran smaller businesses myself, and learned first-hand how many invoices, emails, contracts and spreadsheets even a small company generates.
about_page.why_p2: That combination matters: I understand the code and the systems, but I also know what daily life looks like for the owner of a 5–50 person company — data typed a second and third time because no system talks to the others, and the constant "someone will sort it out later". So when I talk to you, I don't need your business explained to me. We go straight to specifics: what's eating the time, and what can realistically come off your plate.
about_page.how_text: Directly, with no salespeople and no handoffs between departments. One person — me — takes you from the first call, through the audit and implementation, to ongoing care of the working automation. You know exactly who you're talking to at every stage.
not_doing_items: I don't build websites or online stores
I don't implement full ERP systems
I don't take on projects I can't deliver on the agreed timeline
I don't promise funding support until I hold the formal registration for it
